correctness.rationale: For d=2 a rank-deficient pair consists exactly of zero first/second column or equality, giving inclusion-exclusion s^n+2q^n−2q^(2n); reflection and derivative monotonicity give the unique finite optimum, including n=2 at 1/sqrt2. For fixed d, any rank-deficient binary-row set is inside a cube-spanned hyperplane. A pivot-coordinate pairing bounds its cube vertices by 2^(d-1) and the equality classification leaves only x_j=0 and x_i=x_j; all other event bases and pairwise intersections are uniformly exponentially smaller for p near 1/2, including derivatives. The trial solution forces global optimizer localization; strict local convexity gives eventual uniqueness; derivative balance yields Lambert-W correction and failure ratio. Independent n≤5 d=2 exact real ranks corroborate; fixed-width limit is analytic.

evidence: Dexter et al show stochastic rounding can regularize singular values, Jain et al treat square growing dimension at fixed p, and the old fair ±1 matrix result differs from zero-one fixed-width p optimization.

value.rationale: A sharp reliability question for independent stochastic-nearness quantization of a degenerate constant rank-one input: maximal entry entropy p=1/2 is demonstrably suboptimal for restoring rank. The exact fraction/rare-event reduction matters for fixed-width tall rounded matrices and quantifies a real tension not resolved by generic singular-value guarantees.

final_claim: For fixed width d≥2 iid Bernoulli(p) n×d matrix from constant rank-one input, for sufficiently large n there is a unique failure-probability minimizing fraction p=1/2+W(n/(d-1))/(2n)+O_d(log²n/n²), with optimal/midpoint failure ratio (d-1)/(d+1). For d=2, exactly Phi=s^n+2q^n-2q^(2n) and a unique optimizer in (1/2,1) at every n≥2.
limitations: Fixed width d, row count n large, constant input Bernoulli(p), real rank; exact finite-n uniqueness only d=2. No growing-d result or singular-value lower bound.
